$comment: How a frame shows a fish's photo so it keeps the fish (packages/schema/src/image-geometry.ts subjectFrame; the Design Lead's look for each frame: docs of the frames board). For a frame of `ratio` (width over height) and a photo `w` by `h` with the fish's `box` (fractions of the photo from its top-left corner, as `box` and `imgBox` carry it): the frame covers the photo with a window of its shape, which cuts one side of the photo only. The fish's loss is the share of the box's length along that side that falls outside the window. (1) The centred window, if it loses `cut` or less (plus `slack`, so the last bit of a window's edge can't turn exactly `cut` into more); (2) else the window centred on the box, kept inside the photo, if it loses `cut` or less; (3) else the photo whole. No box (null): the centred window, never whole; the site sends a fish's or breed's photo it has no box for with its whole area as its box (x 0, y 0, w 1, h 1), so null is only what an index from before 14 Nov sends. `frame`: {"fit": "cover", "x", "y"} places the window as CSS object-position does (its offset over the room it has to move, 0.5 where it has none), or {"fit": "whole"}. Each box is as the app is sent it (four places, rounded outward from the photo's pixels: boxFractions), and the site decides on those same fractions (subjectFrame is frameOf on them), so both decide alike; positions agree to `tolerance`. Generated by packages/schema/test/photo-crop-vectors.test.ts from the site's rule: edit a case's inputs here (note, w, h, box, ratio), then run UPDATE_VECTORS=1 on that test file, which writes every frame and `cut`; the test fails while the file differs from what the rule gives. The app's tests are to hold its own rule and cut to this file.

clear.$comment: A card's or a head's frame (the Design Lead's frames.md, 14 Nov; the chief of staff): no cut at all, and the fish's box clear of each edge the frame adds by `share` of that side or `points`, whichever is more, the frame being `width` by `height` (points in the app, CSS px on the site, as drawn). (1) The centred window, if its edges inside the photo each lie that far outside the box (`slack` as above); (2) else the window centred on the box, kept inside the photo, if it does; (3) else the photo whole, except for a box the photo cuts already (below). An edge at the photo's own edge counts for nothing: the frame doesn't add it. A box within `ownEdge` of any of the photo's own edges (x or y under it, x + w or y + h over 1 - it, summed as doubles) is cut by the photo already: where (1) and (2) don't clear it, its frame is the lists' rule above (`cases`) on `width` over `height`, whole included, rather than (3) (the Design Lead's frames.md, 15 Nov). No box: centred, never whole. Rows and list tiles keep the lists' rule. Written by the v2 Lab from the app's rule (PhotoFrame.clear); the site's test is to hold its rule to these cases.
